title: Vibration Latency at the Knee in Wistar Rodents
author: Ashleigh Abbott

When holding the tuning fork for testing, don't touch the prongs to prevent vibration damping. To activate vibration hit the top of the prongs near the weights on the palm of your hand. Use roughly the same force and distance of hitting it on your palm to keep consistent throughout the experiment.
Personal Protective Equipment Disposable gloves Face mask (optional) Disposable gown

Materials: Tuning fork (128 hz) Timer (phone timer can be used) Figure 1: Tuning fork at 128 hz used in testing. When holding the tuning fork for testing, don't touch the prongs to prevent vibration damping. To activate vibration hit the top of the prongs near the weights on the palm of your hand. Use roughly the same force and distance of hitting it on your palm to keep consistent throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Acclimate animals to handling
steps.instruction: Acclimate animals to the experimenter and environment before baseline data collection. Ensure behavior room conditions mimic testing conditions.

substeps.instruction: Acclimate animals to the room for 30 minutes prior to starting handling.
Week 1: Perform routine handling acclimation (touching, picking up, general handling) for 5-10 minutes per rat.
Week 2: Acclimate animals to the C-hold and palpation of the knee.
Adjust acclimation time as needed based on age (older rats 15+ months may need longer) and sex (females may be more reactive).

steps.title: Prepare animals for testing
steps.instruction: Prepare the rodents for the vibration latency test to minimize stress and environmental interference.

substeps.instruction: Bring a few rodents into the room at a time to reduce light cycle effects.
Allow animals to acclimate to the testing space in their cages for 30 minutes.
Remove animals from cages one at a time for testing.

steps.title: Position the rodent
steps.instruction: Secure the rodent in a stable position using a C-hold.

substeps.instruction: Handler sits and holds the rodent against their chest in a C-hold.
Position the rodent with the dorsal side toward the handler's chest and the knee facing out.

steps.title: Locate the knee joint space
steps.instruction: Identify the target area for stimulus application once the animal is settled and not squirming.

substeps.instruction: Lightly palpate the knee to locate the joint space.
Identify the 'BB like structure' (fibular head) on the lateral side of the knee to confirm the joint space location.
Note that the joint space may be more cranial than expected depending on rat size and anatomy.

steps.title: Activate and apply tuning fork
steps.instruction: Apply the vibrational stimulus to the anterior aspect of the knee inferior to the patella.

substeps.instruction: Strike the tuning fork approximately 5-7 inches away from the palm of the hand using consistent force; avoid striking it near the rodent to prevent fear response.
Place the bottom surface of the tuning fork on the anterior aspect of the joint space (medial aspect of the knee, inferior to the patella) without touching any other part of the fork.
Hold the tuning fork in place for approximately 10 seconds or until a response is recorded.

steps.title: Record and evaluate response
steps.instruction: Observe the animal and record the type and timing of the response.

substeps.instruction: Identify a Positive Response: Audible vocalization accompanied by visual withdrawal from the stimulus and/or reflexive withdrawal felt by the handler.
Identify an Ambiguous Response: Rat moves, slightly raises, or shakes the leg during or after the 10-second count without vocalizing.
Identify a Negative Response: No movement, shaking, or physical withdrawal after the 10-second count.
If the response is ambiguous, repeat the measurement/application until a positive (X) or negative (O) response is obtained.
Record the specific type of withdrawal (vocalization, visual, or reflexive).

steps.title: Complete multiple trials
steps.instruction: Repeat the testing process to collect a total of 3 trials per rodent.

substeps.instruction: Perform one trial on each animal.
Repeat the application and recording process two more times for each rodent.
Ensure a 30-minute separation between trials on the same rodent.
